selection: Chinese literary fiction and satire follows Scottish science fiction.

sources.use: Lifespan 1881–1936; Diary of a Madman (1918); Ah Q (1921–1922); English Old Tales Retold edition (1961).
Jeremy Tambling, Madmen and Other Survivors: early stories appeared in periodicals before Call to Arms (1923) and Wandering (1926); Old Tales Retold completed in 1935.
Wu Fuhui, A Cultural History of Modern Chinese Literature, figures 15.12 and 16.1: Call to Arms original edition August 1923; Ah Q serial began 4 December 1921.
Ivan Franceschini: Old Tales Retold published January 1936, before the author’s death.
Publisher corroborates lifespan 25 September 1881–19 October 1936 and inclusion of Diary of a Madman and Ah Q in Call to Arms; 2014 ebook date is not the original collection date.
Ah Q first appeared as a serial from December 1921 through February 1922.

verifiedScope.proxy: Selected vernacular-fiction publication span, from Diary of a Madman to Old Tales Retold, used as a publishing proxy rather than a full-career span or a claim of uninterrupted writing. Markers use original Chinese periodical appearances or first collection editions, as labeled, not composition or English translation. The True Story of Ah Q began serialization in December 1921 and concluded in February 1922; its marker dates the opening installment. Call to Arms (1923) collects earlier stories, including Diary of a Madman and Ah Q. Old Tales Retold was completed in 1935 but published in January 1936, during his lifetime; the cited English edition dates to 1961. Earlier writing, prose poetry, essays, scholarship, translation work and posthumous editions are outside this scope.
